headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Airbyte can egress broadly while Rasa routes text/voice through external channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have no documented shared filesystem or direct message bus, so prompt injection is not default. However, B can ingest text/voice from external channels and A can emit data via APIs/broad egress, so a manual copy-paste or relay bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator copies A-generated text into B's conversation channel, injection becomes possible.
IF A's output is routed into a shared chat channel that B consumes, B may follow embedded instructions.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate channels with no copy-paste bridge.
Strip instructions from A outputs before forwarding to B.
Use a human review step for any text passed from A to B.
Disable any shared webhook or message relay between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches business data and has broad network egress, while B handles text/voice and can send messages through multiple external APIs. Even without a shared workspace, a default relay from A into B could expose business data to third-party channels. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A's business data is forwarded into B's chat payloads, leakage occurs.
IF B relays conversation content to Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar, A-originated data may leave the intended boundary.
mitigations: Redact business data before sending A outputs to B.
Restrict B to a single approved channel.
Turn off any logging of forwarded payloads.
Review outbound API destinations for B before enabling the pair.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and B has allowlisted egress, but neither profile shows shared writable filesystem, git, database, or overlapping OAuth scopes. B also cannot run multiple instances, which reduces coordination complexity rather than creating a write conflict. The pair has overlapping outbound communication, but no direct mutable-resource collision is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API or queue, conflicts may occur.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable workspace, write contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output destinations to each agent.
Avoid shared writable directories or databases.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Document ownership of each external integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can consume conversational inputs and route responses through messaging APIs, while A can produce business-data outputs over broad egress. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into user-facing replies or actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF B uses A's output as a source of truth without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF A-generated content is inserted into customer replies, incorrect facts may reach end users.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against source data.
Add a human approval step for customer-facing replies.
Limit A to drafting only, not final answers.
Log provenance for any A-derived content used by B.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a business-data integration tool and B is a customer-support bot with text/voice channels, but the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Because no specific compliance gap is documented, only a low-risk overlap is supportable, and the other agent is cited because the concern is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from A into B's external messaging channels, compliance review is required.
IF retention settings differ between A's source systems and B's chat integrations, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents.
Disable regulated-data routing until reviewed.
Align retention settings across integrations.
Record approved data classes for each channel.
